blindSummary:
This state/province is the only unit in the country that has not enacted any regional LGBTQ+ or gender-identity law, a vacuum maintained across multiple legislatures. A gender-equality bill registered by the centre-left opposition (December 2024) only reached processing on 11 June 2025 after the governing centre-right party abstained and the far-right party voted alone against; the far-right party is on record rejecting LGBTQ+ subsidies in the state/province. The pending law is explicitly framed around halting the documented exodus of LGBT people, especially young ones, from this state/province's rural areas to larger cities.

For a transgender visitor the practical effect of the legislative vacuum is the absence of a dedicated equality office, no institutional hate-crime observatory, and no state/province-specific administrative protocol for responding to gender-motivated incidents. National criminal law still applies and no criminal ban or facility restriction exists in this state/province, so the baseline severity is set by national law. The gap reflects administrative coldness and rural exposure, not any region-specific criminal threat.

A neighbouring state/province at least operated a trans law and an anti-discrimination law before narrowing them; this state/province has never had the framework to narrow - the gap is legislative vacuum versus legislative rollback. The state/province's rural geography compounds the absence of protective infrastructure, and the exodus pattern is documented here rather than being a statute-book gap alone.
blindSourceSummaries: A national news outlet (11 June 2025): the governing centre-right party's abstention let the regional parliament open debate on the centre-left opposition's 76-article equality bill - this state/province remains the only unit in the country with no LGBTQ+ regulation of its own; only the far-right party and two independent members voted against; the opposition sponsor stressed education-sector training, a sanctions regime for non-compliant administrations, and special attention to the rural double discrimination faced by LGBTQ+ people.

A regional outlet (20 December 2024): the centre-left opposition registered a bill expressly framed on stopping the documented exodus of LGBTQ+ people, especially young ones, from the state/province's rural areas to larger cities, and on breaking a wall in regional society; an opposition spokesman told the governing centre-right party there are no more excuses since national law already demands regional development.

A regional newspaper (11 June 2025): the vote on taking up the bill analysed by party - the centre-left opposition, a regionalist bloc, the left, a centrist regional party and a former governing-party member backed it, recalling this state/province is the only unit in the country without its own legislation (a 2021-drafted law remains blocked); the opposition delegate noted rising assaults and hate speech since the far right entered national institutions (a former senior official's rainbow-flag jab); the governing centre-right party held rights are already guaranteed by the constitution and autonomy statute; the far-right party voted against alone; an LGBTQ+ participation council chair warned the law must not be left stuck in process.

A national LGBTQ+ federation's report (September 2025, co-written with a public university; front matter retrieved): a scan of educational-diversity policies across the country's units, listing this state/province among those lacking a regional LGBTQ+ education protocol.
blindLocalsOnly: The exodus pattern itself is resident-facing in its essentials (documented departure of LGBT, especially young, residents to larger cities; no equality office, hate-crime observatory or administrative protocol for residents' complaints), while a visitor's exposure stays governed by national law.
